newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Bosnia mediator Bildt remains in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Bosnia mediator Bildt remains in hospital.

text.p: Swedish politician Carl Bildt, who is overseeing peace efforts in Bosnia, remained in hospital on Monday after being admitted at the weekend with a suspected viral infection, a hospital spokeswoman said.
Bildt, 47, was taken to Danderyds Hospital in Stockholm's northern suburbs on Saturday after collapsing at his home. He was suffering headaches, tiredness and had difficulties speaking.
"He is still here and we are carrying out further tests," a hospital spokeswoman said.
It was unclear how long Bildt would remain in hospital but his condition was seen as not serious.
Bildt, the leader of Sweden's opposition conservative party, the Moderates and Swedish prime minister from 1991-94, returned to Stockholm on Friday to visit his family.
He was originally due to go to London on Sunday and return to Bosnia on Tuesday.
His Sarajevo office has said his illness will not affect day-to-day operations.
Bildt took on the Bosnian mission, where he is the major power's High Representative, after the Moderates lost power to the Social Democrats in a 1991 general election.
Bildt has said he will give up his position in Bosnia and return to Sweden around May this year to lead the Moderates into the next general election in September 1998.
